existing_system_baseline: The existing scenario serving readiness payload used source_commit for both the immutable model workload source and the currently executing serving code revision.

architecture_delta.before: One source_commit field ambiguously represented model provenance and serving runtime code identity.
architecture_delta.after: The compatibility source_commit remains the immutable model source, model_source_commit makes that meaning explicit, and runtime_source_commit independently identifies the serving code revision.
architecture_delta.compatibility: Existing source_commit consumers and historical production intents remain readable; exact runtime matching is enforced only when a new serving process is launched with an expected runtime revision.

implementation.runtime_revision_preflight: A new production serving launch fails before GPU-holder mutation when no exact 40-character runtime source revision is available.
implementation.trace_service_version: The serving OTLP service version now uses runtime_source_commit while model source identity remains an explicit span/readiness attribute boundary.
implementation.legacy_reconcile_behavior: Health reconciliation without an explicit expected runtime revision preserves the prior model-identity contract for already-running historical services.

focused_tests.command_scope: scenario model serving and production intent runtime tests

static_analysis.scope: changed serving, production launcher, and tests

unresolved: The active serving process predates this contract and has not been revision-aligned or revalidated.
No fresh trace links API, durable task handoff, worker, Airflow, data, Spark, MLflow, and serving in one lifecycle.
The complete bounded metric set and three independent low-load controls remain unexecuted.
claim_boundary: This checkpoint proves an additive source-identity contract and repository regression only. It is not live serving identity proof, full S0 acceptance, a benchmark, availability, scale, or production evidence.
